findings.desc: Closeout receipt replay does not prove the current write was canonical. latestValidCloseoutReceipt accepts any historical receipt whose artifactDigest matches current bytes and whose headHash is merely an ancestor; it does not bind the receipt to the commit/change under review or require the receipt to be newly minted with that artifact change. Reverting an artifact manually to previously receipted bytes therefore reuses the old canonical writer claim and passes retention. More generally receiptHash is recomputable from a public salt, so a manual writer can self-assert a canonical writerCommand. This violates CHK-004/CHK-005 manual, replayed, and stale-provenance fail-closed guarantees.

The delivery-context runtime validator accepts semantically invalid payloads that CHK-003 says must fail closed. validatePersistedDeliveryContextPack leaves candidateRouting and validation completely unchecked, does not exact-key or type-check claims, accepts non-string entries in diff.changedFiles/testFiles/evidenceCommands, and does not validate deliveryCheck.ref. A structurally plausible pack such as changedFiles:[42] with arbitrary candidateRouting/validation and extra claims fields is treated as trusted, while the smoke only tests authorityDone=true. Tighten the persisted schema to the producer contract and add adversarial cases.

Receipt replay defeats the claimed manual/stale-write rejection. latestValidCloseoutReceipt filters all historical receipts for the path and returns any matching valid record, so after canonical A then canonical B, a manual revert of the artifact to A is accepted under the old receipt even though the latest write was not canonical. Reproduced against dist: receipts [A@2026-01-01,B@2026-01-02] plus current summary.json=A returned acceptedTimestamp=2026-01-01. Bind receipts to the actual write/commit and reject superseded/replayed receipts (including copied/reordered receipt-ledger entries).

The 15-intent evidence overstates CLI/integration coverage. CHK-004 is type=cli and requires canonical parent_ledger_rollup_set output, but closeout-trust-smoke never invokes that handler/CLI; it calls store.writeProofStoryParentLedgerRollup plus autoCommitStoryMetadata directly. Likewise none of the newly wired validate, done_required_validate, delivery_check_set/waiver, evaluate_save, summary_set, delivery_context_pack, or live_smoke_transcript handler paths are executed. The smoke can stay green if a handler omits or passes the wrong closeoutArtifactPaths. Add at least one real CLI/handler regression for parent_ledger_rollup_set and table-driven integration coverage for every registered canonical writer path; wire this high-risk smoke into routine test discovery/evidence.

Trusted artifact runtime schemas accept missing required timestamps and semantically invalid delivery-context fields. Repro after the story build: calling validateTrustedMilestoneLedger with createdAt removed, validateTrustedSlicePlan with updatedAt removed, and validateTrustedParentLedgerRollup with createdAt removed all return successfully; validatePersistedDeliveryContextPack also accepts changedFiles:[42], testFiles:[42], evidenceCommands:[{}], and deliveryCheck.ref as a string. This contradicts CHK-003 edge/adversarial and means malformed persisted payloads can cross the new trust boundary. Require/validate createdAt+updatedAt (including ISO shape), validate optional typed fields/semantic relationships, require string arrays for delivery paths/commands, validate ref null/object and exact claims shape, and add negative regressions.
